definitions.explanation: Spread out with gaps in between, not dense or closely packed. Describes things that are few and far between.

examples.japanese: {客|きゃく}は{疎|まば}らだった。
{雨|あめ}が{疎|まば}らに{降|ふ}っている。
{平日|へいじつ}の{午前中|ごぜんちゅう}は{人|ひと}が{疎|まば}らで、ゆっくり{買|か}い{物|もの}ができる。
examples.english: On weekday mornings the crowd is thin, so you can shop at your leisure.

notes:
USAGE:
Often written in hiragana (まばら). Describes people, objects, hair, vegetation, or anything that should be denser but has noticeable gaps. Can modify nouns with な or be used predicatively.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人|ひと}が{疎|まば}ら (few people, thinly populated)
- {疎|まば}らな{拍手|はくしゅ} (scattered applause)
- {髪|かみ}が{疎|まば}ら (thin/sparse hair)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {少|すく}ない: few — simply indicates small quantity
- ちらほら: here and there — adverb describing scattered occurrence
